SRC-253:R001.text: SAIPEN has a documented canonical Auto-Doctor contract (SELF_HEALING_CONTINUATION): typed failure classes that each produce a canonical action, reusing existing owners

SRC-253:R002.text: cc can invoke authorized recovery automatically inside the normal continuation path, without a separate operator command

SRC-253:R003.text: The reference STALE_PASS conformance condition recovers without a manual saipen validate

SRC-253:R004.text: CURRENT_PASS is verified after recovery rather than assumed; a zero exit code alone is insufficient

SRC-253:R005.text: The original Work resumes automatically after a successful recovery, without a second cc

SRC-253:R006.text: The recovery stays bound to the real original operator command: no new operator decision is synthesized

SRC-253:R007.text: No duplicate execution occurs across the original cc, the recovery, validation and the resumed Work

SRC-253:R008.text: Unsafe failures preserve STOP, NO_GO, operator and integrity boundaries and stop with an exact canonical reason

SRC-253:R009.text: Recovery attempts are bounded and idempotent: one automatic revalidation per chain, no cc-validate-cc loop

SRC-253:R010.text: Race conditions and restart behavior are tested (concurrent writer, crash between recovery and resume)

SRC-253:R011.text: Health checks add no unacceptable overhead to a healthy cc; expensive validation runs only when the contract requires it

SRC-253:R012.text: ZAICODE has a structured integration contract for Doctor stages; ZAICODE code itself changes only under its own admission

SRC-253:R013.text: A real host acceptance test proves the user-facing behavior when separately authorized

SRC-253:R014.text: Existing protocol regression gates remain passing

SRC-253:R015.text: Relevant recovery and provenance evidence is preserved and survives interruption
